scenario: Ice-core dust measurements are only logged when concentration exceeds 180 ppb (instrument noise floor). Logged measurements show a mean of 280 ppb (σ=45 ppb). Palaeoclimatologists wish to estimate the true mean dust concentration across all ice-core depths.

data.description: Observed statistics among values exceeding the reporting threshold

values.note: Only observations above the threshold enter the record

question: (a) Assuming dust concentration follows a normal distribution with σ=45 ppb, solve numerically for the true population mean μ satisfying E[X | X > 180] = 280. (b) What fraction of all dust concentration events lie above the 180 ppb threshold? (c) By how much (in ppb) does the observed truncated mean overstate the true μ? (d) Explain the inferential risk of using the observed mean directly as an estimate of μ.

ground_truth.explanation: The observed mean 280 ppb is E[X|X>180], the expectation of a truncated-normal distribution. Solving μ+σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=280 numerically yields μ=278.32619 ppb. Only 98.6% of all events are recorded; the observed mean overstates the true mean by 1.67381 ppb. Using the observed mean directly as μ would lead to systematic over-estimation of the severity/magnitude of the process.

naive_answer: The true mean dust concentration is 280 ppb because that is the average of all available measurements.
naive_trap: Only events above 180 ppb are recorded; the observed mean is a conditional expectation E[X|X>180], not the population mean. It always exceeds μ whenever the threshold is binding.
reasoning_trace: (1) Define α=(t−μ)/σ where t=180, σ=45. (2) Truncated-normal expectation: E[X|X>t]=μ+σ·φ(α)/Φ̄(α). (3) Set equal to 280 and solve for μ via brentq on [-945.0, 279.9999]. (4) Solution: μ=278.32619 ppb. (5) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=Φ̄((180−278.32619)/45)=0.98556.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 280,45,180
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-25*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=300)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-278.32619)<0.005, f'mu={mu_sol:.5f}'
assert abs(frac-0.98556)<0.005, f'frac={frac:.5f}'
assert mu_sol < obs
assert abs((obs-mu_sol)-1.67381)<0.01
